bans: no ranking is scored against an outcome it also predicts (atoms-freed)
every arm reported in full, never the best
three outcome states -- improved, inert, undecided -- and a wall hit is never folded into inert
no loop iteration started from a truncated level
config.definition: rank by look_ahead.freed per vertex added, ties broken by his decreasing admission-degree order, restricted to candidates of at most n_new_max vertices; on a stall raise n_new_max (his own escape) and re-rank; at the last rung propose his second strategy, many_then_trim
config.held_out_state: our 375-level accumulator, 403 vertices, which equals his v403e2112 literally (zero differing vertices, re-derived 2026-09-11)
config.if_the_held_out_map_is_signal_free: then the rule is scored by outcome on ONE held-out row -- one bit -- and no map stands behind it. That is written here BEFORE the run so it is anticipated rather than salvaged. A column of zeros at A403 is the STRONGER outcome: it sits beside a demonstrated four-orbit success from the same state, making 'single-orbit expansion never works, even where a four-set does' a fact about single moves rather than about that state.
config.outcome: clause 2(b) is met only by |M| <= 374; {M} growth at fixed |M| and fixed rung in an iteration that added vertices is clause 2(c) and is recorded separately
config.target: the primary decision asks target = incumbent - 1 = 373 atoms, i.e. |M| <= 374 vertices, which is exactly clause 2(b)
